THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE  COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC-K:5559  MFA No.200829 of 2021  JUDGMENT

The claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the II Additional District and Sessions Judge and MACT, Raichur (henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.366/2018, vide judgment and award dated 06.02.2020.

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Judge and MACT, Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The claimant suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 02.08.2017 when the car in which he was travelling over turned due to the rash and negligent driving by its driver.
As a result, the claimant suffered injuries and was shifted to Government hospital, Devadurga, where he was treated for nearly nine days.
He claimed he was 24 years old at the time of accident and was earning Rs.9,000/- per month apart from Rs.1,50,000/- per annum from agriculture.
He therefore, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the car.
3. The claim petition was resisted by the insurer of the car who denied the accident as well as the injuries suffered by the claimant in the accident.
It contended that the compensation claimed by the claimant was excessive.
Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as P.W.1 and he marked Exs.P.1 to P.11.

He also examined a doctor as P.W.2, who deposed that the claimant had suffered four injuries namely:
i. Comminuted fracture of shaft of left femur.
 ii. Blunt injury to abdomen  iii. Head injury  iv. Fracture of right ankle
P.W.2 depose that the fracture of left femur was not united properly.
He deposed that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 25% to the whole body.

sentences.text: 5. Based on the oral and documentary evidence adduced before the Tribunal, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car.
It held that the claimant suffered fracture of left femur and fracture of right medial malleolus bones and other injuries.

As against the evidence of P.W.2, it held that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body and NC: 2023:KHC-K:5559 it considered the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.9,000/- per month and awarded the following compensation:
 Sl. Head Amount  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Pain and suffering 40,000/-
 2. Medical expenses 81,795/-
 3. Food, nourishment and 15,000/-
 conveyance

4 . Attendant charges 10,000/-
 5. Loss of income during laid 18,000/-
 up period

6. Loss of future earnings 1,94,400/-
 7. Loss of amenities 20,000/-
 8.
Future medical expenses 20,000/-

Total compensation 3,99,195/-
 Rounded off 3,99,200/-
6.
It directed the insurer to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded, the claimant is in appeal.

7. Learned counsel for the claimant contended that the claimant was an agricultural labourer as well as agriculturist and hence, comminuted fracture of left femur which was not united and the fracture of the right medial malleolus, must NC: 2023:KHC-K:5559 have left the claimant completely disabled.
He submitted that though P.W.2 was not the doctor who treated the claimant, yet the disability certificate issued by him was based on the radiological reports.
He also submitted that the claimant had suffered shortening of the left limb by 1 cm and that there was a restriction in the movement of the ankle.
He further submitted that the notional income of the claimant must have been considered at a sum of Rs.10,250/- per month.
8. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not call for any enhancement.
9. The insurer has not challenged the negligence on the part of the driver of the car.
It has also not contested the injuries suffered by the claimant in the accident.
The wound certificate at Ex.P.3 and the discharge cards at Exs.P.6 and P.7 indicate that the claimant had suffered comminuted facture of left femur and fracture of right medial malleolus bones.

P.W.2, who deposed that the fracture of the Maunddin @ Mainuddin S/O Bava Sab vs Amaresh S/O Sharanappa And Anr on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170558297/
3 left femur was malunited and the interlocking nails were in situ.

sentences.text: In addition to this, the claimant had suffered other injuries.

Having regard to the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5559 nature of avocation of the claimant and the fact that he was an agriculturist, the fractures of two vital bones must have affected his function as an agriculturist.
Consequently, the assessment of disability at 10% was on the lower side and based on the evidence on record, this Court considers it appropriate to assess the disability at 15% to the whole body.
As rightly contended the learned counsel for the claimant the notional income of the claimant must have been considered at a sum of Rs.10,250/- per month.

If the above is given effect to, the claimant would be entitled to enhanced compensation which is re-determined as follows:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Pain and suffering 60,000/-

2 . Medical expenses 81,795/-
 3. Nourished food, conveyance 55,000/-
 and attendant charges

4. Loss of amenities 40,000/-
 5. Future medical expenses 20,000/-
 6. Loss of income due to 3,32,100/-
 disability  (Rs.10,250/- x 12 x 15% x  18)
 7. Loss of income during laid up 30,750/-
 period  Total 6,19,645/-
 NC: 2023:KHC-K:5559 10.
In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.
The compensation of Rs.3,99,200/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to Rs.6,19,645/-.

11. The enhanced compensation shall be paid by the insurer of the car along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization, excluding the interest for the delayed period of 335 days.
12. The insurer of the car shall deposit the enhanced compensation and interest before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
13. Upon deposit, out of the enhanced compensation and accrued interest, 50% of the same shall be deposited in the name of the claimant in any nationalized bank for a period of three years.
